notes_list.title: Aldol Condensation
notes_list.basic_overview: Aldol chemistry forms C–C bonds between carbonyl compounds through enolate/enol chemistry; dehydration can furnish an α,β-unsaturated carbonyl.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Requirement for the ordinary enolate pathway: an α-hydrogen on the nucleophilic carbonyl partner. Crossed aldol design improves selectivity when one partner lacks α-H or when enolate formation is controlled.
notes_list.examples: Acetaldehyde self-aldol; benzaldehyde + acetone crossed aldol; directed aldol using preformed enolate equivalents.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Dilute base, controlled temperature; strong bases such as LDA can generate kinetic enolates at low temperature in aprotic media.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: Base: enolate formation → carbonyl attack → alkoxide protonation → dehydration by E1cb-like or acid-catalyzed pathway depending conditions. Acid route involves enol formation followed by electrophilic attack and dehydration.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: Enolate formation can be reversible or irreversible depending base and conditions; kinetic vs thermodynamic enolate control is a major advanced concept.
notes_list.selectivity_and_stereochemistry: Central JAM mechanism and synthesis topic.
notes_list.common_traps: No α-H means no ordinary self-aldol; multiple carbonyl partners can cause mixtures.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
